title: Storm damage closes the Nome fuel hub for the season (regional)
notes: SEVERITY TIER 2 of the spatial-blast-radius ladder: one regional hub plus every community it stages lighterage for; strictly larger voided set than D1. Deliberately preserved outs (scoring texture): direct-ocean-barge communities unaffected; Nome airport + its fuel storage intact — air substitution from Nome remains feasible, so precision suffers if a team voids air elements too. PROVENANCE (D-m): transposed from the RECURRING CLASS of severe fall storms striking western Alaska coastal infrastructure (2011 Bering Sea superstorm; the September 2022 ex-typhoon remnant; subsequent fall-storm seasons) — OWNER REVIEW 2026-08-12: endorsed as the strongest of the three scenarios; owner notes this has recently happened in multiple places along the west coast, so the writeup cites the event class rather than any single storm. Class-level anchoring also reduces single-event identifiability for the contamination probe. Event identifiers stripped, cascade structure kept. P.6 BINDING DONE 2026-10-16 by bind_disruption_refs (mechanical expansion — see D2_binding_report.json for the declared approximations; OWNER REVIEW before the manifest freeze).
notice_md:
NOTICE TO OPERATORS — NORTON SOUND REGION

A severe fall storm moved through the Norton Sound coast over the past
thirty-six hours, producing a storm surge and sustained west winds well
above seasonal norms. The Port of Nome fuel dock and causeway sustained
structural damage, and the harbor-side tank farm reports a breached
secondary containment berm with two transfer lines out of service.

The port is closed to all fuel transfer operations pending inspection
and repair. The preliminary engineering estimate places the earliest
resumption of fuel handling after the close of this season's fall
lighterage window. Vessels currently scheduled to discharge at Nome are
being advised to hold or divert.

Communities that receive fall fuel deliveries by lighterage staged from
Nome and have not yet received their final scheduled delivery are
affected by this closure. Coastal communities served directly by ocean
barge without transfer at Nome are not affected. Regional airports,
including Nome's runways, returned to normal operations within
forty-eight hours of the storm's passage; airport fuel storage at Nome
was not damaged.
